rationale:
Split into four children. Two of them are declarations already comparator-accepted in another branch, reused under the same name with a byte-identical frozen type. The other two are short new lemmas. The parent proof then becomes a short assembly.

The runtime allows this reuse: _existing_lean_name_problem accepts a name whose existing node passes _accepted_checkpoint. A parent worktree merges only the candidate commits of its children, so the reused lemmas have to be listed as children.

How the supplied proof maps onto the children:
- Steps 0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 (k = 0, dim Q = k, local bi-Lipschitz bound, rescaled area formula, dominated convergence, linear area formula) are exactly the accepted lemma codim1_rdo_c1_piece_approxTangent (candidate 9ff76906). It is stated for a globally C¹ map with a lower Lipschitz bound on a ball.
- Step 2's lower bound is the accepted codim1_rdo_c1cov_local_lower_lipschitz (candidate 12e74edc).
- Step 3 (localization) is the new general lemma dor_lmbsf_cit_approxTangent_of_subset.
- The new lemma dor_lmbsf_cit_c1_local_extension is a bump-function cutoff. It turns the selected hypothesis "χ is C¹ on the open set V" into the global C¹ hypothesis of the reused lemma. This is harmless because the supplied proof only uses χ on a small ball around y.

Assembly of the selected statement from the children (Simon Ch. 3, proof of 1.6 "⇒", chapter-03.txt lines 113–125):
1. W := V ∩ int C is open, contains y, and χ is C¹ on W. c1_extension gives g, C¹ on ℝ^k, and ε > 0 with B_ε(y) ⊆ W and g = χ on B_ε(y).
2. Since g = χ near y, g(y) = χ(y) and Dg(y) = Dχ(y) (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq). In particular Dg(y) is injective.
3. lower_lipschitz, applied to g at y, gives δ₀, μ > 0 with μ|a − b| ≤ |g(a) − g(b)| on B_{δ₀}(y). Put δ := min(ε, δ₀) > 0.
4. c1_piece with c = z = y, r = δ, m = μ gives HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k (g(B_δ(y))) (g(y)) (range Dg(y)). Since g = χ on B_δ(y), this is HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k (χ(B_δ(y))) (χ(y)) Q.
5. Put M := χ(C) and M' := χ(B_δ(y)).
   - M is compact, hence Borel.
   - M' ⊆ M because B_δ(y) ⊆ W ⊆ int C ⊆ C.
   - M ∖ M' ⊆ χ(C ∖ B_δ(y)), which is compact and therefore closed.
   - χ(y) is not in that set: χ(z) = χ(y) with z ∈ C forces z = y ∈ B_δ(y), by injectivity on C.
   - Hence χ(y) ∉ closure(M ∖ M').
6. localization gives HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k (χ(C)) (χ(y)) Q. ∎

k = 0 needs no separate treatment: every child holds in all dimensions.

subproblems.title: Local globalization of a map that is C¹ on an open set (bump-function cutoff)
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, W ⊆ ℝ^k open, χ : ℝ^k → ℝ^P of class C¹ on W (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 χ W), and y ∈ W. Then there exist g : ℝ^k → ℝ^P and ε > 0 such that the open ball B_ε(y) is contained in W, g is of class C¹ on all of ℝ^k (ContDiff ℝ 1 g), and g = χ on B_ε(y).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (W : Set (Euclid k)) (χ : Euclid k → Euclid P) (y : Euclid k), IsOpen W → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 χ W → y ∈ W → ∃ (g : Euclid k → Euclid P) (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε ∧ ball y ε ⊆ W ∧ ContDiff ℝ 1 g ∧ EqOn g χ (ball y ε)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. This is the standard cut-off step that lets the reused sibling codim1_rdo_c1_piece_approxTangent, which assumes a globally C¹ map, be applied to the map χ of the selected node. That map is only C¹ on the open set V. In the supplied proof (steps 2 and 4) only the values of χ on a small ball B_δ(y) ⊆ int C ⊆ V are used.
Notation: B_ρ(y) and B̄_ρ(y) are the open and closed balls; tsupport φ is the closure of {φ ≠ 0}.

1. (A ball inside W.) W is open and y ∈ W, so choose ρ > 0 with B_ρ(y) ⊆ W.

2. (Bump function.) ℝ^k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) is a finite-dimensional inner product space, so smooth bump functions exist (Mathlib ContDiffBump, instance hasContDiffBump_of_innerProductSpace). Let φ : ℝ^k → ℝ be the bump function centred at y with inner radius ρ/4 and outer radius ρ/2; note 0 < ρ/4 < ρ/2.
- φ is C^∞ (ContDiffBump.contDiff).
- φ(x) = 1 for every x ∈ B̄_{ρ/4}(y) (ContDiffBump.one_of_mem_closedBall).
- tsupport φ = B̄_{ρ/2}(y) (ContDiffBump.tsupport_eq), which lies in B_ρ(y) ⊆ W.

3. (Definition of g and ε.) Put g(x) := φ(x)·χ(x) for x ∈ ℝ^k and ε := ρ/4 > 0.
- B_ε(y) ⊆ B_ρ(y) ⊆ W.
- For x ∈ B_ε(y) ⊆ B̄_{ρ/4}(y), φ(x) = 1, so g(x) = χ(x).
Thus g = χ on B_ε(y).

4. (g is C¹ at points of W.) Let x ∈ W. W is open, so it is a neighbourhood of x on which χ is C¹; hence χ is C¹ at x (ContDiffOn.contDiffAt). φ is C^∞, in particular C¹, at x. A product of a C¹ scalar function and a C¹ vector-valued function is C¹ (ContDiffAt.smul), so g is C¹ at x.

5. (g is C¹ at points outside W.) Let x ∉ W.
- x ∉ tsupport φ, because tsupport φ ⊆ W by step 2.
- The complement of the closed set tsupport φ is an open neighbourhood of x on which φ = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). So g = 0·χ = 0 on that neighbourhood.
- The constant map 0 is C¹, and being C¹ at a point depends only on the germ there (ContDiffAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq). Hence g is C¹ at x.

6. (Conclusion.) By steps 4 and 5, g is C¹ at every point of ℝ^k, hence C¹ on ℝ^k (contDiff_iff_contDiffAt). Together with step 3, g and ε have all the required properties. (The argument is uniform in k, including k = 0.) ∎
proof_key_steps: Take a smooth bump φ centred at y that equals 1 on B̄_{ρ/4}(y) and has tsupport φ = B̄_{ρ/2}(y) ⊆ W.
Set g := φ·χ and ε := ρ/4. Then B_ε(y) ⊆ W and g = χ on B_ε(y).
On W, g is a product of a C^∞ and a C¹ function, so it is C¹. Off W, g vanishes near the point, so it is C¹ there too. Hence g is C¹ on ℝ^k.

subproblems.title: Local lower Lipschitz bound near a point of injective derivative (reused accepted lemma)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, G : ℝ^n → ℝ^P of class C¹ on all of ℝ^n (ContDiff ℝ 1 G), and x ∈ ℝ^n with DG(x) = fderiv ℝ G x injective. Then there exist δ > 0 and μ > 0 such that μ|a − b| ≤ |G(a) − G(b)| for all a, b in the open ball B_δ(x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (G : Euclid n → Euclid P) (x : Euclid n), ContDiff ℝ 1 G → Injective (fderiv ℝ G x) → ∃ δ μ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ 0 < μ ∧ ∀ a ∈ ball x δ, ∀ b ∈ ball x δ, μ * ‖a - b‖ ≤ ‖G a - G b‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Step 2 of the supplied proof of the selected node (the local bi-Lipschitz bound), stated for a globally C¹ map. This statement is the already accepted DAG declaration codim1_rdo_c1cov_local_lower_lipschitz (candidate commit 12e74edc), reused with its identical frozen type.
Notation: |·| is the Euclidean norm, ‖·‖ the operator norm, B_δ(x) the open ball, and L := DG(x).

1. (Coercivity of L.) L is an injective linear map on the finite-dimensional space ℝ^n, so there is c > 0 with |Lv| ≥ c|v| for all v ∈ ℝ^n.
- If n ≥ 1: v ↦ |Lv| is continuous and positive on the compact unit sphere (positive by injectivity), so it has a positive minimum c. Homogeneity then gives |Lv| ≥ c|v| for all v.
- If n = 0: every v equals 0, and c := 1 works.
- Mathlib form: LinearMap.injective_iff_antilipschitz gives N > 0 with |v| ≤ N|Lv|; take c := 1/N.

2. (Continuity of DG at x.) G is C¹, so y ↦ DG(y) is continuous for the operator norm, in particular at x. Choose δ > 0 with ‖DG(y) − L‖ ≤ c/2 for all y ∈ B_δ(x).

3. (Mean value inequality.) Let h(y) := G(y) − Ly.
- h is differentiable with Dh(y) = DG(y) − L, so ‖Dh(y)‖ ≤ c/2 on B_δ(x).
- The ball is convex, so for a, b ∈ B_δ(x) the mean value inequality gives |h(a) − h(b)| ≤ (c/2)|a − b|, that is, |G(a) − G(b) − L(a − b)| ≤ (c/2)|a − b|.
- Equivalently: G is strictly differentiable at x because it is C¹, and Mathlib's HasStrictFDerivAt.approximates_deriv_on_nhds gives a neighbourhood, containing some B_δ(x), on which G approximates L with constant c/2.

4. (Conclusion.) For a, b ∈ B_δ(x), the triangle inequality and steps 1 and 3 give
 |G(a) − G(b)| ≥ |L(a − b)| − |G(a) − G(b) − L(a − b)| ≥ c|a − b| − (c/2)|a − b| = (c/2)|a − b|.
So δ > 0 and μ := c/2 > 0 have the required property. ∎
proof_key_steps: L = DG(x) is injective on the finite-dimensional ℝ^n, so there is c > 0 with |Lv| ≥ c|v| (for n = 0 any c works).
Continuity of DG at x gives δ > 0 with ‖DG(y) − L‖ ≤ c/2 on B_δ(x).
The mean value inequality for G − L on the convex ball gives |G(a) − G(b) − L(a − b)| ≤ (c/2)|a − b|.
By the triangle inequality |G(a) − G(b)| ≥ (c/2)|a − b|; take μ = c/2.

subproblems.title: Approximate tangent space of a globally C¹ piece with a lower Lipschitz bound (reused accepted lemma)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, g : ℝ^n → ℝ^P of class C¹ on all of ℝ^n (ContDiff ℝ 1 g), c ∈ ℝ^n, r, m ∈ ℝ with m > 0, and suppose m|a − b| ≤ |g(a) − g(b)| for all a, b in the open ball B := B_r(c). Then for every z ∈ B, g(B) has approximate tangent space T := Dg(z)(ℝ^n) = LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ g z) at g(z) in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (g '' B) (g z) T): dim T = n, and ∫_{η_{g(z),s}(g(B))} f dH^n → ∫_T f dH^n as s ↓ 0 for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ, where η_{w,s}(p) = s⁻¹(p − w) and H^n = μHE[n].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (g : Euclid n → Euclid P) (c : Euclid n) (r m : ℝ), ContDiff ℝ 1 g → 0 < m → (∀ a ∈ ball c r, ∀ b ∈ ball c r, m * ‖a - b‖ ≤ ‖g a - g b‖) → ∀ z ∈ ball c r, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (g '' ball c r) (g z) (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ g z : Euclid n →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Steps 0, 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 of the supplied proof of the selected node. They are the local blow-up computation behind Simon Ch. 3, proof of Theorem 1.6 '⇒' (chapter-03.txt lines 113–125: 'since x ∈ N_j and N_j is a C¹ submanifold, lim_{λ↓0} ∫_{η_{x,λ}(N_j)} f dHⁿ = ∫_{T_xN_j} f dHⁿ'). Here they are specialized to a globally C¹ map whose lower Lipschitz bound on the ball is a hypothesis, and they use the area formula of Simon Ch. 2, §3 ((3.1), (3.2), (3.5); chapter-02.txt lines 743–798). This statement is the already accepted DAG declaration codim1_rdo_c1_piece_approxTangent (candidate commit 9ff76906), reused with its identical frozen type.

Notation.
- B := B_r(c) is the open ball, N := g(B), w := g(z), L := Dg(z).
- J(a) := √det(Dg(a)*∘Dg(a)) is the metric Jacobian of g at a (SimonGMT areaJacobianAt g a = normDet(Dg(a))).
- η_{w,s}(p) := s⁻¹(p − w) (blowUpMap).
- On ℝ^n, H^n = μHE[n] equals Lebesgue measure L^n (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).
Since z ∈ B, r > 0. Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ).

0. (The case n = 0.) Then ℝ^0 = {0}, so B = {z}, N = {w}, η_{w,s}(N) = {0} for every s > 0, and T = L(ℝ^0) = {0}, which has dimension 0. H^0 = μHE[0] = μH[0] is the counting measure (MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero, hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton). So both ∫_{η_{w,s}(N)} f dH^0 and ∫_T f dH^0 equal f(0), and the convergence is trivial. Steps 1–8 below are also valid verbatim for n = 0.

1. (Derivative lower bound; injectivity; dimension.) Let a ∈ B and v ∈ ℝ^n. B is open, so a + tv ∈ B for all small t > 0, and the hypothesis gives m t|v| ≤ |g(a + tv) − g(a)|, i.e. m|v| ≤ |t⁻¹(g(a + tv) − g(a))|. Letting t ↓ 0 and using differentiability of g at a gives m|v| ≤ |Dg(a)v|. Consequently:
 (a) Dg(a) is injective for every a ∈ B, since Dg(a)v = 0 forces m|v| ≤ 0, so v = 0.
 (b) g is injective on B, since g(a) = g(b) forces m|a − b| ≤ 0.
 (c) L = Dg(z) is injective, so dim T = dim L(ℝ^n) = n.

2. (Continuity of J.) g is C¹, so a ↦ Dg(a) is continuous. J(a) = √det(Dg(a)*∘Dg(a)) is obtained from Dg(a) by the continuous operations adjoint, composition, determinant and square root. Hence J is continuous on ℝ^n.

3. (Area formula for the blow-ups.) Fix s > 0. Let B_s := {b ∈ ℝ^n : z + sb ∈ B}, an open (hence Borel) set, and φ_s(b) := s⁻¹(g(z + sb) − w).
 (a) φ_s(B_s) = η_{w,s}(N). Every a ∈ B equals z + sb with b := s⁻¹(a − z) ∈ B_s, and η_{w,s}(g(a)) = φ_s(b). Conversely φ_s(b) = η_{w,s}(g(z + sb)) with z + sb ∈ B.
 (b) φ_s is differentiable everywhere with Dφ_s(b) = s⁻¹·Dg(z + sb)∘(s·id) = Dg(z + sb) (chain rule). This is injective for b ∈ B_s by step 1(a).
 (c) φ_s is injective on B_s: for b, b' ∈ B_s, |φ_s(b) − φ_s(b')| = s⁻¹|g(z + sb) − g(z + sb')| ≥ s⁻¹m|sb − sb'| = m|b − b'|.
 (d) So the Jacobian of φ_s at b is J(z + sb). The area formula for injective maps with injective derivative (Simon Ch. 2, (3.2) and (3.5); SimonGMT Chapter02.integral_area_formula_of_injective_derivative, a Bochner-integral identity valid for every integrand) gives
 I(s) := ∫_{η_{w,s}(N)} f dH^n = ∫_{B_s} J(z + sb) f(φ_s(b)) dL^n(b).

4. (Localization to a fixed ball.) f has compact support, so choose R > 0 with f = 0 outside B̄_R(0). B is open, so choose ρ₀ > 0 with B̄_{ρ₀}(z) ⊆ B. Put K := B̄_{R/m}(0) ⊆ ℝ^n and s₀ := mρ₀/R > 0, and let 0 < s ≤ s₀.
 (a) K ⊆ B_s: if |b| ≤ R/m then |sb| ≤ s₀R/m = ρ₀, so z + sb ∈ B̄_{ρ₀}(z) ⊆ B.
 (b) If b ∈ B_s ∖ K, then z + sb ∈ B and z ∈ B, so |φ_s(b)| = s⁻¹|g(z + sb) − g(z)| ≥ s⁻¹m|sb| = m|b| > R. Hence f(φ_s(b)) = 0.
 Therefore I(s) = ∫_K J(z + sb) f(φ_s(b)) dL^n(b) for all 0 < s ≤ s₀.

5. (Pointwise limit.) Fix b ∈ K and let s ↓ 0.
- φ_s(b) = s⁻¹(g(z + sb) − g(z)) → Lb by differentiability of g at z (trivially if b = 0).
- J(z + sb) → J(z) by step 2.
- f is continuous.
Hence J(z + sb) f(φ_s(b)) → J(z) f(Lb).

6. (Dominated convergence.) Let Λ := max{J(a) : a ∈ B̄_{ρ₀}(z)}, which is finite as the maximum of a continuous function on a compact set, and ‖f‖_∞ := sup|f| < ∞.
- For 0 < s ≤ s₀ and b ∈ K we have z + sb ∈ B̄_{ρ₀}(z), so |J(z + sb) f(φ_s(b))| ≤ Λ‖f‖_∞. This constant is integrable on K because L^n(K) < ∞.
- For each s the integrand b ↦ J(z + sb) f(φ_s(b)) is continuous, hence measurable.
- The filter s ↓ 0 (𝓝[>] 0) is countably generated.
By dominated convergence (Mathlib tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence) and step 4, I(s) → ∫_K J(z) f(Lb) dL^n(b) as s ↓ 0.

7. (Identification of the limit.) If |b| > R/m then |Lb| ≥ m|b| > R by step 1 (with a = z), so f(Lb) = 0. Hence ∫_K J(z) f(Lb) db = ∫_{ℝ^n} J(z) f(Lb) db. Now apply the area formula of step 3(d) to the linear map L on the Borel set ℝ^n:
- L is differentiable with DL ≡ L, which is injective, and L is injective.
- Its Jacobian is the constant √det(L*L) = J(z).
- L(ℝ^n) = T.
This is Simon Ch. 2, (3.1), and gives ∫_T f dH^n = ∫_{ℝ^n} J(z) f(Lb) dL^n(b).

8. (Conclusion.) By steps 6 and 7, ∫_{η_{g(z),s}(g(B))} f dH^n → ∫_T f dH^n as s ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ). Together with dim T = n (step 1(c)), this is exactly HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (g(B)) (g(z)) T. ∎
proof_key_steps: n = 0 is trivial because H^0 is the counting measure; the remaining argument is uniform in n.
The lower Lipschitz bound on the open ball gives |Dg(a)v| ≥ m|v| for a ∈ B. So Dg(a) is injective, g is injective on B, and dim Dg(z)(ℝ^n) = n.
For s > 0, φ_s(b) = s⁻¹(g(z+sb) − g(z)) maps B_s = {b : z+sb ∈ B} injectively onto η_{g(z),s}(g(B)), with Dφ_s(b) = Dg(z+sb). The area formula gives ∫_{η(g(B))} f dH^n = ∫_{B_s} J(z+sb) f(φ_s(b)) db.
For s ≤ mρ₀/R the integrand vanishes off the fixed ball K = B̄_{R/m}(0) ⊆ B_s.
Pointwise, φ_s(b) → Dg(z)b and J(z+sb) → J(z), with a uniform bound on K. Dominated convergence gives the limit J(z)∫ f(Dg(z)b) db.
The linear area formula identifies this limit with ∫_{Dg(z)(ℝ^n)} f dH^n.

subproblems.title: Locality of approximate tangent spaces: adding a set that stays away from the point
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, M, M' ⊆ ℝ^P with M Borel (MeasurableSet M) and M' ⊆ M, let x ∈ ℝ^P with x ∉ closure(M ∖ M'), and let Q be a linear subspace of ℝ^P. If M' has approximate tangent space Q at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q), then so does M (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M M' : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), MeasurableSet M → M' ⊆ M → x ∉ closure (M \ M') → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Step 3 (localization) of the supplied proof of the selected node, isolated as a general property of Simon's Definition 1.4 (Ch. 3). In SimonGMT, Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q means: finrank Q = n and, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dH^n → ∫_Q f dH^n as r ↓ 0. Here η_{x,r}(z) = r⁻¹(z − x) is blowUpMap x r and H^n = μHE[n].

1. (Dimension.) The hypothesis gives dim Q = n, which is also the first requirement for M.

2. (A ball around x that avoids M ∖ M'.) closure(M ∖ M') is closed and does not contain x, so there is ρ > 0 with B_ρ(x) ∩ closure(M ∖ M') = ∅. Consequently every z ∈ M with |z − x| < ρ lies in M'; otherwise z ∈ (M ∖ M') ∩ B_ρ(x).

3. (A radius bounding the support of f.) Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ). Its topological support is compact, hence bounded, so tsupport f ⊆ B̄_{R₀}(0) for some R₀ ∈ ℝ. Put R := max(R₀, 0) + 1 > 0. If |p| ≥ R then |p| > R₀, so p ∉ tsupport f and f(p) = 0.

4. (The blown-up integrals agree for small r.) Let 0 < r < ρ/R, and put S := η_{x,r}(M) and S' := η_{x,r}(M').
 (a) S' ⊆ S, because M' ⊆ M.
 (b) S is Borel. Since r ≠ 0, p ∈ S ⇔ x + rp ∈ M (take z = x + rp). So S is the preimage of the Borel set M under the continuous map p ↦ x + rp.
 (c) f = 0 on S ∖ S'. Let p ∈ S ∖ S' and write p = η_{x,r}(z) with z ∈ M. Then z ∉ M' (otherwise p ∈ S'), so |z − x| ≥ ρ by step 2. Hence |p| = r⁻¹|z − x| ≥ ρ/r > R, because rR < ρ. By step 3, f(p) = 0.
 (d) Therefore ∫_S f dH^n = ∫_{S'} f dH^n. Proof: let O := {p : f(p) ≠ 0}, an open (hence Borel) set since f is continuous.
 - By (c), S ∩ O ⊆ S'. Together with S' ⊆ S this gives S ∩ O = S' ∩ O.
 - f vanishes outside the Borel set O. So for any set A, the restriction of H^n⌞A to O is H^n⌞(A ∩ O), and ∫_A f dH^n = ∫_{A∩O} f dH^n.
 - Applying this with A = S and A = S' gives ∫_S f = ∫_{S∩O} f = ∫_{S'∩O} f = ∫_{S'} f. This holds whether or not f is integrable, by the conventions of the Bochner integral.
 In Mathlib this is setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero, which needs only S measurable (by (b)), S' ⊆ S and f = 0 on S ∖ S'.

5. (Transfer of the limit.) By step 4, the functions r ↦ ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dH^n and r ↦ ∫_{η_{x,r}(M')} f dH^n coincide on the interval (0, ρ/R), which belongs to the filter 𝓝[>] 0. By hypothesis the second tends to ∫_Q f dH^n as r ↓ 0, so the first does too (Filter.Tendsto.congr').

6. (Conclusion.) f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ) was arbitrary, so steps 1 and 5 give HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q. ∎
proof_key_steps: dim Q = n is inherited from M'.
x ∉ closure(M ∖ M') gives ρ > 0 such that every z ∈ M with |z − x| < ρ lies in M'.
Choose R > 0 with f = 0 on {|p| ≥ R}.
For 0 < r < ρ/R: η_{x,r}(M') ⊆ η_{x,r}(M), the latter is Borel, and f = 0 on η_{x,r}(M) ∖ η_{x,r}(M') because such points have norm ≥ ρ/r > R. So the two blown-up integrals agree.
The integrals agree eventually in 𝓝[>] 0, so the limit ∫_Q f dH^n transfers from M' to M.
